speaker: Doctor
text: When did you first notice the yellowish discoloration on the newborn's skin? Is the baby feeding well and having regular wet diapers and bowel movements?

speaker: Patient
text: 5-day-old male newborn. The newborn's mother reports that her child has developed yellowish discoloration of the skin that started from the face and then spread to the trunk since the past day. There have been no changes in his bowel habits or urination. The baby was born full-term at 38 weeks’ gestation via an uncomplicated vaginal delivery and has been exclusively breastfed every 2–3 hours.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Are the stools pale or clay-colored, and has the baby been taking adequate feeds? I will also check for any hepatosplenomegaly.
REQUEST TEST: Total and Direct Bilirubin

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Total Bilirubin: 7 mg/dL, Direct Bilirubin: 0.6 mg/dL

speaker: Doctor
text: The bilirubin levels are mildly elevated but consistent with physiologic jaundice, given the unconjugated pattern and normal feeding. Does the baby have a family history of hemolytic conditions or G6PD deficiency, and have you noticed any dark urine or lethargy?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Yellowish discoloration of the skin. I also have Discoloration started from the face then spread to the trunk, Scleral icterus noted.

speaker: Doctor
text: The progression of jaundice from face to trunk and the presence of scleral icterus are consistent with physiologic jaundice in a 5-day-old. Given the normal bilirubin levels and lack of other concerning symptoms, no further immediate intervention is required. DIAGNOSIS READY: Physiologic Jaundice
